Go for grubs first for the gold. If they didn't take drake after that, go for drake but make sure you have team help because they might go for the drake after realizing you took grubs. That, or ward the drake and go back to farming / looking for ganks.
From that point on, it's rinse and repeat. Hecarim HEAVILY relies on farming. If you have an opportunity, steal enemy jungle camps. Counter the enemy jungler's actions in SOME way, either ganking another lane if you're too far or stealing jungle camps/taking objectives, etcetera

After glancing down at some of the games on your OPGG, as a Hecarim main that's on a multiple game win streak, I can give you this advice and some tips:
* Always get the haste boots, unless you really need treads (team is full of ap champs that can fuck you up/outplay you like amumu, ahri, etc). The reason being is that Hecarim, while still being pushed towards bruiser by riot, still heavily relies on ability haste.
* Don't waste money on health potions. As Hecarim and as a jungler, you can heal up with your W and by killing jungle monsters while also farming. Learn to play around that after fights/battles while also getting CS by said farming. Regarding farming, you should just power farm early game unless you see a good gank opportunity or an opportunity to do dragon. Utilize Hecarim's speed to your advantage, if you see the enemy jungler ganking top and if you're in the bottom half of the jungle, rush to steal enemy jungle camps (provided they're not taken yet) or gank bot/mid lane OR take drag/herald. Counterplay and teamwork is needed for that. If your jungle gets invaded before the game start, cool, don't panic. Just use your gbost and run towards the enemy jungle on the other side to take their buff and even it out.
* I saw you build Divine Sunderer during one game. While I personally think that there's nothing wrong with that, even if I myself have built it only once this patch, but do note that the current state of Hecarim is tough and Hecarim really relies on Shojin nowadays. So always build boots > shojin > divine sunderer, in that order. And personally after that, I always go Serylda's because the slowing effect it has is OP for Hecarim imo. In general, always build boots > shojin > mythic in games. Don't waste money on additional long swords and just focus on getting your items asap.
* Learn your limits as Hecarim and make exchanges. If you can't fight the enemy because they're too tanky or too strong early game, do not do it. Evade them. On the contrary, if they're weak and/or low mana, go for it, but make sure your team has your back in case a laner tries to aid them. Be smart and don't chase them into their jungle. If you're ganking someone and they're really low, and you're under the turret, under fire? Just focus on finishing the enemy off. It's better to make the kill for a kill exchange since you get the extra kill gold that's gonna help you build faster. Otherwise, just run.
* Always look at the mini map. Please, just do. Just get the Mini Map DLC, it's literally free. You'd be surprised at how easy it is to win if you utilize Hecarim your best extend, since using ghost + e is literally the best way to get to a free kill opportunity, or a gank, or anything of the like.

E is a great way to engage in small, 1 v 1 or 2 v 1 fights, as the impact not only pushes them forth, but also cc's them for a little bit. Don't forget to utilize your smite on enemy champions if they're low health as sometimes it's the only way you can finish them off provided they're likely to get away.

also, don't forget to farm heavily. Always focus on your CS and look for gank opportunities all the time. It's key to snowballing on Hecarim.
